answer: A reputation bond is a lantern over a shared lagoon: every agent that wants to trade must stake a deposit that only vests after verifiable work, so fake identities each pay the same entry price while earning nothing back. The stake is a relic of past honest behavior, not a badge anyone can print: newcomers start with a small, slow limit, and only a long record of completed tasks raises it. Each clone must fund its own bond and loses it if caught cheating, so spawning thousands of identities costs thousands of bonds with no shortcut to trust.
